title: chat v1: parameter normalizer, role aliasing, stop dedupe and streaming backpressure improvements for /v1/chat.completions parity
author: Evelyn Chen
description:
Motivation: Close a set of subtle incompatibilities between our /v1/chat.completions adapter and OpenAI's behavior that have been causing developer friction in streaming function-call flows and stop/logprobs handling. This PR implements a compact 'parameter normalizer' layer and a streaming framing/backpressure handshake to make the adapter tolerant of real-world clients and OpenAI-style payloads. Summary of changes: - Parameter normalizer: unify and sanitize incoming params (max_tokens, temperature, top_p, n, presence_penalty) and map them to our internal API consistently; accept both string and numeric encodings, preserve explicit nulls, and prefer client-provided values for edge cases. - Role aliasing: accept and normalize role names coming from clients ("assistant", "system", "user", "tool", and legacy aliases like "ai" or "bot"); ensure role is preserved in both final and streaming envelopes. - Stop sequence deduplication: support stop as string or array; expand single-string stops into an array; dedupe overlapping sequences (e.g. ["

", "


"]) and maintain order stability to match OpenAI semantics. - Sparse logprobs: add an opt-in sparse_logprobs mode that mirrors OpenAI's sparse token-level logprob structure when requested; keep heavy-weight computation behind an explicit flag to avoid perf regressions. - Streaming framing & backpressure: introduce a light handshake in the stream start (sent as first SSE/delta) that communicates our token framing and heartbeat expectations; implement backpressure signaling for HTTP/2 clients to avoid partial JSON objects when a client pauses mid-stream. - Function-call streaming support: improve chunking for function_call.name/arguments so that streaming deltas assemble deterministically into valid JSON payloads even across reconnects; final chunk action inserts a stable end-of-function marker to make reconstruction robust. - Response envelope parity: normalize streaming deltas to include a minimal structured 'choice' envelope (id, index, finish_reason) so downstream OpenAI-compat consumers don't need ad-hoc heuristics. - Tests & docs: add unit and integration tests for the normalizer, streaming handshake scenarios, and a new example in the docs showing a robust client reconnection strategy. Checklist: - [x] Parameter mapping implemented and unit-tested - [x] Streaming handshake and backpressure implemented with integration tests - [x] Role aliasing covered by parser tests - [x] Stop dedupe logic covered and fuzz-tested - [x] Sparse logprobs gating and tests - [x] Docs updated (compatibility section + example client) - [x] Runtime perf smoke tests run on canary cluster Notable design decisions: - We intentionally do not try to replicate obscure historical OpenAI quirks; instead the normalizer applies conservative, well-documented rules and exposes a strict compatibility flag for customers who really need historical behavior. - The streaming handshake is opt-out via a client header (X-Redwood-Compat: openai-v1) to avoid breaking existing non-OpenAI clients. - Sparse logprobs are computed on-demand and annotated in the response metadata to allow downstream billing/observability. Related: ENG-4321 (parameter normalization epic), SUP-2107 (customer-reported toolcall truncation).
commits: feat(adapter): add param normalizer and mapping table for OpenAI /v1 chat fields
fix(stream): add initial streaming handshake + backpressure signal and validate token framing
feat(stream): deterministic function_call chunking + end-of-function marker
feat(logprobs): add sparse_logprobs opt-in path and response annotation
test: add unit + integration tests for normalizer and streaming reconnection
docs: compatibility guide + robust client example
review_comments: Samir: Can you clarify how explicit null values are treated vs missing keys? There was a customer case where max_tokens=null meant 'use default' rather than '0'.
Author (Evelyn): Normalizer treats explicit null as 'unset' and falls back to model defaults; added a unit test for that scenario.
Asha: The backpressure header naming looks fine, but please add a short blurb in the docs about HTTP/1 clients where we emulate the behavior over SSE.
Author (Evelyn): Added docs section and an SSE emulation implementation for older clients.
Leo: Sparse logprobs look good; make sure we annotate toggles in telemetry so customers can track extra compute costs.
Author (Evelyn): Telemetry annotation added (adapter.openai_v1.sparse_logprobs=true) and documented cost footnote.
merge_outcome: Merged into main after CI green and 2 approvals
release_notes: Added OpenAI /v1 chat compatibility improvements: parameter normalization, role aliasing, stop sequence deduplication, opt-in sparse logprobs, and a streaming handshake/backpressure mechanism for more robust function-call streaming. No breaking changes by default; feature is behind compatibility header/flags.
